question: If 25% of (P + Q) = 75% of (P - Q), then find the ratio P: Q.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Given 25% of (P + Q) = 75% of (P − Q).

Taking the inverse ratio: (P + Q) / (P − Q) = 75% / 25% = 3 / 1

Applying the Componendo and Dividendo rule:

P / Q = (3 + 1) / (3 − 1)

⇒ P / Q = 4 / 2 = 2 / 1

**∴ The correct answer is 2 : 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

25% of (P + Q) = 75% of (P − Q)

 P (2 parts) Q (1 part) P + Q (3 parts) P − Q (1 part) 
• 
• 
• 
• Ratio P : Q = 2 : 1 

**Calculations:**

⇒ (25 / 100) × (P + Q) = (75 / 100) × (P − Q)

⇒ 1 × (P + Q) = 3 × (P − Q)

⇒ P + Q = 3P − 3Q

Bringing all P terms to one side and Q terms to the other:

⇒ Q + 3Q = 3P − P

⇒ 4Q = 2P

⇒ P / Q = 4 / 2

⇒ P : Q = 2 : 1

**∴ The correct answer is 2 : 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Componendo and Dividendo

If a / b = c / d, then (a + b) / (a − b) = (c + d) / (c − d). This rule is extremely useful for rapidly solving equations that involve sums and differences of the same two variables.

Inverse Ratio Logic

If A% of X = B% of Y, the ratio of the variables is inversely proportional to their respective percentages. Therefore, X / Y = B / A.

Percentage Simplification

Converting standard percentages to simple fractions (e.g., 25% = 1 / 4, 75% = 3 / 4) makes cross-multiplication faster and prevents errors with larger numerical values.
